chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya Al-Halabi, from Ibn Muskan, from Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the boys. So he said: 'Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was asked about the boys and the children, so he said: Allah is more Knowing with what they were doing.'
ai.seo_question: What is the fate of children who die before reaching the age of accountability in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of Zurarah to Imam al-Baqir, clarifies that the fate of children who die before reaching *bulugh* (age of accountability) is not automatically determined by their status but is subject to Allah’s knowledge of their potential deeds (*amal*) had they matured. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that divine justice accounts for latent potential, distinguishing this from the general principle that 'no soul bears the burden of another.'

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Yahya Al Halby, from Ibn Muskan, from Zurara who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about the boys. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was asked about the boys and the children, so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is more Knowing with what they were doing’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Nadr ibn al-Suwayd from Yahya al-Halabiy from ibn Muskan from Zurarah who has said the following: “

I asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the children, and he said, ‘The Messenger of Allah was asked about the children and infants, and he replied, “Allah knows best about what they had been doing.’””
